kf: **Chronic severe eczema of sun-exposed skin** due to abnormal sensitivity to UVB, often UVA and sometimes visible light.
Typically **older fair-skinned men (60+)** in the UK; also younger people with darker skin and atopic eczema.
Sharp cut-off at collar and sleeve lines, sparing behind ears, eyelid folds and under the chin.
Up to about three-quarters have positive patch tests, especially to **Compositae**, fragrance and sunscreen filters.
Refer for phototesting and patch testing; strict photoprotection, allergen avoidance, emollients and topical steroids.
myths: **"Sunscreen will solve it"**: sunscreen allergy is common and visible light may be involved.
patho_lead: CAD behaves like an **allergic contact eczema to the patient's own UV-altered skin**.

mech.t: UV alters an endogenous skin protein, creating a new antigen.
A delayed-type hypersensitivity develops, as in allergic contact dermatitis.
With time, smaller UV doses (and visible light) trigger eczema.
Co-existing Compositae, fragrance and sunscreen allergies keep it going.

histo: Spongiotic dermatitis; in severe cases dense dermal lymphocytes mimicking lymphoma (actinic reticuloid).
comp: Erythroderma, severe impact on quality of life, social isolation.
